personal.name: Zachariah Ayers
personal.title: Principal Software Engineer
personal.headline: C#, .NET, SQL Server and AI agents
personal.summary: Modernizes the systems businesses depend on without breaking them, and designs the platforms engineers build with. Currently on contract with Northrop Grumman: 40+ legacy applications moved to C# and .NET 8, and a release pipeline that cut deploys from weeks to minutes. Earlier, architect at AmeriSave Mortgage: led the move to Azure Red Hat OpenShift, built the company's micro-frontend framework and project generator, led its move to TypeScript, and built a federated GraphQL data layer. Builds AI agents and MCP servers into his own products. Shipping production software since 2013.
personal.story: He builds and runs the software a business depends on, whether it is brand new or decades old.

experience.summary: Independent software company: contract engineering for clients, and its own products.

engagements.name: Northrop Grumman (contract)
highlights: Designed the architecture, SQL Server data layer and integrations for 40+ VB6 applications moved to C# and .NET 8, with no regressions after cutover; about 200 people use them daily.
Built the release pipeline on Azure DevOps: deploys went from weeks to minutes, with checks on every branch, automated test suites and integration tests.

Built the AI engineering layer Northrop's developers adopted over several iterations: AI agents, MCP servers and a full harness of plugins, skills and rules that taught AI coding tools the team's stack, code and database.
Set up an on-premises AI inference server and built the team's own AI agent into its business-facing applications, so business users could ask questions securely.
Delivered the full port under estimate, with a documented handoff.

engagements.name: Powerbuilding Holdings Corp, New York
highlights: Took over the whole application for a training, nutrition and health-tracking platform with a coach side: two Flutter apps, NestJS services, a Django back end, AWS, and Azure OpenAI features.

engagements.name: Gamut, Timelapse+ and Wrapmate
highlights: Gamut: built a licensing system to protect its color grades: file encryption, a licensing server, and plugins for Adobe Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve and Final Cut Pro.
Timelapse+: built an export from Lightroom Classic straight into a DaVinci Resolve project (Lua, Python).
Wrapmate: built a real-time 3D wrap configurator for the VW ID.Buzz, tied into its store (React, TypeScript, Three.js, WebGL, Node).

roles.title: Software Architect and Software Development Manager

highlights: Lead architect for the move to Azure Red Hat OpenShift: microservices deployed on every push, so new hires shipped a live change on their first day. Led the team that trained the engineers on it.
Built AMCUI, the company's micro-frontend framework with Storybook component libraries, and AMCLI, its project generator; led AmeriSave's move to TypeScript.
Built a federated GraphQL layer over the company's data, so business users reached it themselves through Power BI instead of asking developers for SQL queries.

Built much of the rewrite of Aussie, the automated underwriting system or AUS (a rules-based engine with early AI integrations), from ColdFusion 9 to Java Spring Boot and Angular, with zero regressions; then joined the core leadership team that drove it to completion.
Led a team of 6 and reviewed pull requests on the large efforts, including the customer-facing AUS Portal; trained the whole 60-person engineering department (6 teams) in Agile and Jira.

roles.title: Lead Software Engineer and Engineering Manager

experience.summary: Started as a combined mechanical and software engineer; later managed 2 developers.
highlights: Built RabCab, order-to-floor automation: customers designed cabinetry, booths and kiosks in a web configurator, and approved orders flowed through engineering to the shop floor with no manual drafting, leaving engineers free for custom work.
Extended AutoCAD's ObjectARX SDK in C# with custom 3D entities, and kept inventory and costs in sync between the add-in and the website.
Surveyed stores and prepared remodel plans, then built AutoCAD plug-ins that sped up the team's whole workflow.
Placed GPS-tagged 3D photos inside the drawings and generated step-through 3D walkthroughs in AutoCAD; used with clients for before-and-after views.

Built Pantheon, an AutoCAD add-in (VB.NET) that drew framing members straight from the structural engineers' numbers; small configuration choices generated the parts, and drafters finished the polish.

productsNote: Built with hand-written code and AI coding agents working in parallel.
